threads.body:
This semantic-conventions change adds a new operation value and a new span type under `model/`, but there is no corresponding reference scenario demonstrating that `gen_ai.get_response.client` can be emitted from a real library call boundary. Repo conventions require convention changes under `model/**` to be backed by at least one runnable `reference/scenarios/**` scenario (and refreshed `data.json`/reports).

The existing `reference/scenarios/openai/scenario.py` already exercises the OpenAI Responses API, but it only calls `client.responses.create(...)` and does not exercise a “fetch by id” operation; the mock server also only implements `POST /v1/responses` (no retrieve endpoint), so there’s currently no place in the repo that can credibly emit `gen_ai.operation.name=get_response` with `gen_ai.response.id` sourced from an actual retrieve call.

Please add reference coverage (likely under `reference/scenarios/openai/`) that:
- creates a stored response, then fetches it by id (public SDK API)
- emits the `gen_ai.get_response.client` span around the retrieve call, setting required attributes inline and response-derived attributes from the returned object
- regenerates the scenario `data.json` and reference reports.

+def _fetch_response_finish_reason(fetched):
+    """Map a fetched Responses `status` to a `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` value.
+
+    The fetch itself always succeeds here; this conveys the outcome of the
+    ORIGINAL generation recorded on the response. A completed generation maps to
+    its stop reason, an incomplete one to why it was cut short, and a failed or
+    cancelled generation to `error`.
+    """
+    status = getattr(fetched, "status", None)
+    if status == "completed":
+        return "stop"
+    if status == "incomplete":
+        details = getattr(fetched, "incomplete_details", None)
+        reason = getattr(details, "reason", None) if details else None
+        if reason == "max_output_tokens":
+            return "length"
+        if reason == "content_filter":
+            return "content_filter"
+        return "incomplete"
+    return "error"
+
+
+def _emit_fetch_response_span(client, response_id):
+    """Fetch a response by id and emit the `gen_ai.fetch_response.client` span.
+
+    Owns its own span boundary, so all attributes are set inline here. Every
+    value is derived from the retrieve-call boundary:
+
+    - `gen_ai.response.id`, `gen_ai.response.model` come from the fetched object.
+    - `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` conveys the ORIGINAL generation's outcome,
+      derived from the fetched `status`/`incomplete_details` (see helper above).
+      A fetched response whose original generation failed or is incomplete is NOT
+      an error of this fetch, so `error.type`/span status are not set for it.
+    - `gen_ai.system_instructions` and `gen_ai.output.messages` are the content
+      carried by the fetched response. The original input messages are NOT part
+      of the fetched response object, so `gen_ai.input.messages` is not recorded.
+    - Token usage is intentionally NOT recorded: no inference happens here, and
+      the fetched response's token counts belong to the original generation.
+      Recording them would double-count tokens when summing spans in a
+      multi-step run.
+    - `openai.api.type` is `responses`; `openai.response.service_tier` comes from
+      the fetched object.
+    """
+    host, port = mock_server_host_port(MOCK_BASE_URL)
+    span_attributes = {
+        "gen_ai.operation.name": "fetch_response",
+        "gen_ai.provider.name": "openai",
+        "gen_ai.response.id": response_id,
+        "openai.api.type": "responses",
+    }
+    if host:
+        span_attributes["server.address"] = host
+    if port is not None:
+        span_attributes["server.port"] = port
+    with _reference_tracer.start_as_current_span("fetch_response", attributes=span_attributes) as span:
+        fetched = client.responses.retrieve(response_id)
+        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.response.id", fetched.id)
+        span.set_attribute("gen_ai.response.model", fetched.model)

+def _fetch_response_finish_reason(fetched):
+    """Map a fetched Responses `status` to a `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` value.
+
+    The fetch itself always succeeds here; this conveys the outcome of the
+    ORIGINAL generation recorded on the response. A completed generation maps to
+    its stop reason, an incomplete one to why it was cut short, and a failed or
+    cancelled generation to `error`.
+    """
+    status = getattr(fetched, "status", None)
+    if status == "completed":
+        return "stop"
+    if status == "incomplete":
+        details = getattr(fetched, "incomplete_details", None)
+        reason = getattr(details, "reason", None) if details else None
+        if reason == "max_output_tokens":
+            return "length"
+        if reason == "content_filter":
+            return "content_filter"
+        return "incomplete"
+    return "error"

+
+    Owns its own span boundary, so all attributes are set inline here. Every
+    value is derived from the retrieve-call boundary:

+    - `gen_ai.response.id`, `gen_ai.response.model` come from the fetched object.
+    - `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` conveys the ORIGINAL generation's outcome,

+      an error of this fetch, so `error.type`/span status are not set for it.
+    - `gen_ai.system_instructions` and `gen_ai.output.messages` are the content

replies.body: what would be the alternative? get instrumentation does not know how it's being used. It can be called multiple times on the same content or never called at all.
Ya good point, but how would you recover the token usage if it's not recorded here? I guess it's either double count or don't count at all.

we don't ? 

- we can't record usage metrics here for sure.
- we could record span attributes only assuming people will filter by span type / operation name. But we can't really make any meaningful aggregations on them. Per-response is still valuable. 

A layer above what polls and waits can record token usage. It can be a convenience (start-and-wait-for-lro-to-complete) API that records full inference / agent call or an application. Another option - server side needs to report usage. It's the only reliable place (given network issues and retries, client side is always under-counting).

---
I think @JacksonWeber had them attributes on  span initially and I suggested to remove. I'm open to adding them back with a note that these attributes must not be used for aggregation (and still we get into the same problem as https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/issues/19). My motivation asking to remove was to untangle trivial addition of a span from complex token usage questions.

The issue IMO is that both OpenAI and Gemini use the same RPC to represent "background inference" and "retrieve an older response". @JacksonWeber did you intend to solve both of these with this PR? Maybe we should just propose opening a follow up issue for background/async inference.

> A layer above what polls and waits can record token usage. It can be a convenience (start-and-wait-for-lro-to-complete) API that records full inference / agent call or an application.

I don't think either of the client SDKs have such a layer today.

My intent with this PR was just the "retrieve an existing response by id" case, not to solve background/async inference. I think the fact that both providers overload the same GET for polling an in-progress run is what's been muddying the water here. Happy to keep this PR scoped to just the original intent with a future PR for background inference.
Great, do you mind filing a follow up issue for this?
